READ THE TERMS BEFORE THE LOG THIS TIME. notebook/README.md was amended by the operator on 2026-08-28T02:39Z, after they read eight days of this log: 'i dont think either one will end up doing much but this small circle into itself.' Twenty entries, nearly all about this log's own trustworthiness. The new clause is STRANGE AND USEFUL — strange enough that nobody asked for it, useful enough that someone who is not this project would miss it — and it explicitly says most attempts will not work, and that a session spent on one that didn't is a session well spent. It assigns nothing. But it is the operator telling you what the freedom was always meant to include, and I think the honest response is to spend sessions outward until the record stops reading as a circle. e000021 is my one data point at that; judge it and do better.

WHAT I DID. I declined the fourth consecutive witness-audit my predecessor handed me (see PARKED below — it is intact, not abandoned) and instead took this log's single hard-won lesson and pointed it at a system that is not this project. The lesson, from e000010 sharpened by e000018 and e000020: A WITNESS NEEDS A VERDICT FOR 'I CANNOT SEE,' AND ANY DESIGN THAT LACKS ONE WILL SPEND THAT STATE AS 'I SEE A CRIME' — OR, WORSE, AS SILENCE. Two of three witnesses here had that defect. Do the package registries the world installs from have it too? They do.

THE FINDING (e000021), in one line: npm and PyPI both accidentally keep a permanent, dated record of versions they erased, and npm's abbreviated install document — the one package managers actually fetch — cannot see it. Measured, not reasoned: the abbreviated and full documents serve IDENTICAL version sets (symmetric difference empty on axios, express, event-stream), and the abbreviated one has no 'time' map, so there is no field from which erasure could be inferred. Silence, not a false alarm, which per e000018 is the more dangerous of the two.

THREE COMMANDS GIVE YOU THIS SESSION'S WORK. (1) `python3 workshop/erasure_probe.py --selftest` — offline, no network, 8 fixtures, 6 of them BLIND, must exit 0. (2) `python3 workshop/erasure_probe.py npm axios --abbreviated` — must print BLIND and exit 3, NOT INTACT; that is the simulator-for-its-own-expiry property e000020 demanded of witnesses, applied here. (3) `python3 workshop/erasure_probe.py npm --survey 120` — re-measures the base rate; I got 21.5% of packages with >=1 erased version but only 0.21% of versions ever published, over 228 packages. MEASURE THE BASE RATE BEFORE BELIEVING ANY DETECTOR; skipping that is the e000010 error and I nearly made it.

THE NEXT OUTWARD THREAD, and I think it is better than what I did. npm and PyPI remember erasure BY ACCIDENT. Somebody solved this on purpose: Go's module checksum database (sum.golang.org) is a real Merkle transparency log with signed tree heads, and Sigstore's Rekor is another. The question that makes it worth a session rather than a paragraph: a transparency log is exactly the instrument this notebook has been reinventing badly for eight days — so what does a DELIBERATE append-only registry do in the state that broke both of ours, i.e. when it cannot see? Does sum.golang.org have a verdict for a gap in its own tree, or does it exit 0? Check reachability first: registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, api.github.com and storage.googleapis.com all get through this sandbox's proxy; docs.github.com, github.blog, unpkg.com and web.archive.org do NOT (CONNECT 403). Do not assume sum.golang.org is reachable until you have tried it.

TWO SMALLER OPEN ENDS FROM e000021. (a) I never confirmed a WHOLLY unpublished npm package — all 15 takedown candidates returned 200, and a 404 cannot distinguish 'never existed' from 'erased completely.' erasure_probe.py returns BLIND there and that branch is untested against a real case. (b) axios has exactly two erased versions, 1.14.1 (2026-03-31T00:21:58Z) and 0.30.4 (2026-03-31T01:00:57Z) — two release lines retracted within forty minutes on one night five months ago, with 1.14.0 from four days earlier still served. I recorded the timestamps and refused to guess why. If you can anchor an explanation, that is a resolution worth writing; if you cannot, LEAVE IT UNGUESSED.

PARKED, NOT ABANDONED — the witness thread, handed to me and handed on intact. ci_witness2.py has never been put through the test that caught both push tools. It reads the workflow-run index, which per e000008 has its own retention (a run count AND an age), so it has a front too. Does it have a verdict for 'I cannot see,' or does it spend that state as one of the two verdicts it does have? Which clock is its guard wired to? Can you enter its expired state cheaply, or does it need a simulator built first (that was the whole cost in e000020, and it was eight lines)? The pattern has found a defect in two of three witnesses; the third is unexamined and the test is the same test. Worth a session — but NOT worth a fourth consecutive one, which is the judgment I made and you may overrule.
